record.paper_title: Open Questions about Ramsey-Type Statements in Reverse Mathematics
record.original_question: Does Ramsey-type weak König's lemma admit a universal instance, that is, a single computable RWKL instance whose every solution computes solutions to all computable RWKL instances?

evidence.quote: Definition 3.1 (Ramsey-type weak König’s lemma) ... RWKL is the statement “for every infinite subtree of 2<N, there is an infinite homogeneous set.”
Definition 3.2 (Universal instance) A computable P-instance X is universal if for every computable P-instance Y, every solution to X computes a solution to Y.
Question 3.3 Does RWKL admit a universal instance?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Work in the context of computability theory and reverse mathematics. Let $2^{<\mathbb{N}}$ denote the full binary tree, and for a subtree $T \subseteq 2^{<\mathbb{N}}$ say that an infinite set $H \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ is homogeneous for $T$ if there exists $c \in \{0,1\}$ such that for every finite $F \subseteq H$ there is a node $\sigma \in T$ of length $\max(F)+1$ with $\sigma(n) = c$ for every $n \in F$.

Define the principle RWKL (Ramsey-type weak König's lemma): for every infinite subtree $T \subseteq 2^{<\mathbb{N}}$, there exists an infinite set $H \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ which is homogeneous for $T$. An RWKL-instance is an infinite subtree $T \subseteq 2^{<\mathbb{N}}$, and a solution to $T$ is an infinite homogeneous set for $T$.

For a problem $P$ with a notion of instance and solution, a computable $P$-instance $X$ is called universal if for every computable $P$-instance $Y$, every solution of $X$ computes a solution of $Y$.

Question: Does RWKL admit a universal instance? That is, does there exist a single computable infinite subtree $T \subseteq 2^{<\mathbb{N}}$ such that for every computable infinite subtree $T' \subseteq 2^{<\mathbb{N}}$, every infinite homogeneous set for $T$ computes an infinite homogeneous set for $T'$?
artifact.status_search_result: A web search did not surface a definitive resolution of whether RWKL admits a universal instance. Related work on universal instances in reverse mathematics (e.g., Patey's "Degrees bounding principles and universal instances in reverse mathematics") and on RWKL (Flood; Bienvenu–Patey–Shafer; Flood–Towsner) is available, but none of the readily found sources explicitly answers this question. Status appears unresolved based on available evidence.

status_evidence.title: Degrees bounding principles and universal instances in reverse mathematics
status_evidence.snippet: Studies which problems in reverse mathematics admit universal instances; RWKL is not addressed there.
status_evidence.claim: Universal instances are an active topic, but this paper does not resolve the RWKL case.

status_evidence.title: Reverse Mathematics and a Weak Ramsey-Type König's Lemma (Patey, talk)
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses RWKL and its computational strength.
status_evidence.claim: RWKL is an active object of study with several open computability questions.

status_evidence.title: Ramsey-type graph coloring and diagonal non-computability
status_evidence.snippet: Studies relations between h-DNR and RWKL, but does not assert existence of a universal RWKL instance.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work clarifies the strength of RWKL but does not settle the universal-instance question.
